Production compose uses:
- Caddyfile.production with `{$API_DOMAIN}` etc. If set to `.localhost` domains, Caddy will try Let's Encrypt for `app.localhost` which will fail (can't get public cert for .localhost). Actually Caddy treats .localhost specially? Caddy has a rule: if the host is "localhost" or has a .localhost TLD, it does not attempt ACME and instead uses internal CA? Let me recall. Caddy documentation: "Caddy automatically uses its internal CA for localhost, .localhost, and IP addresses." Yes! Caddy will not try to get certificates for domains ending in `.localhost` — it uses the internal CA. Actually I think that behavior applies. Let me confirm: Caddy's `tls` automation will skip ACME for hosts that are localhost. I believe Caddy has special handling: hosts that are not public (like .localhost, .internal, IPs) get internal certs. Yes, Caddy 2.5+ automatically uses internal issuer for localhost domains.

So production compose may work with .localhost domains. However, production compose has backend-wms, pg-error-parser (needs docker socket — fine), wireguard (needs NET_ADMIN and /lib/modules — in container it may fail). Wireguard requires kernel modules which likely aren't available; the container may fail to start. That could cause `docker compose up` to error but others continue. Wireguard has `restart: unless-stopped` and may keep crashing. Compose up returns once containers are created/started; a crashing container doesn't necessarily fail `up`. Actually `docker compose up -d` returns 0 even if some container exits.

The dev compose does not include wireguard and backend-wms and pg-error-parser is there but uses docker.sock. Dev compose is simpler and explicitly "with Caddy local HTTPS".

The installation guide's Quick Start specifically says `cd deployment && docker-compose up -d --build`, which uses docker-compose.yml (production). But README notes production requires domain names or use localhost with certificates.

Given the guide is the primary source, and it says to use `docker-compose up -d --build`, I'll try that. But I'm worried about wireguard and resource. Let me first check /lib/modules and whether we can run privileged containers.

Also `qgis/pg_service.conf.template` needs to be copied to `pg_service.conf`? The README says QGIS setup requires copying it, but compose auto-generates pg_service.conf at startup using env vars (in the command). So not needed. Actually the compose command writes pg_service.conf. Let me check pg_service.conf.template.
